front_blocks.md: Define **image editing**.

back_blocks.md: Image editing is the process of **manipulating images and changing them to suit the user's end goal**.

cards.front_md: Define **image editing**.
cards.back_md: Image editing is the process of **manipulating images and changing them to suit the user's end goal**.

front_blocks.md: Name four image editing techniques.

back_blocks.md: Techniques include **placing an image with precision**, **resizing**, **cropping**, **rotating**, **reflecting (flipping)**, **adjusting brightness and contrast**, and **grouping and layering**.

cards.front_md: Name four image editing techniques.
cards.back_md: Techniques include **placing an image with precision**, **resizing**, **cropping**, **rotating**, **reflecting (flipping)**, **adjusting brightness and contrast**, and **grouping and layering**.

front_blocks.md: How can an image be placed with precision?

back_blocks.md: By **selecting the image and dragging it** to the desired location, or by using **coordinates or alignment tools** where the software allows.

cards.front_md: How can an image be placed with precision?
cards.back_md: By **selecting the image and dragging it** to the desired location, or by using **coordinates or alignment tools** where the software allows.

front_blocks.md: What does maintaining the aspect ratio mean?

back_blocks.md: It means the image's **width and height change at the same rate**, which **prevents distortion**.

cards.front_md: What does maintaining the aspect ratio mean?
cards.back_md: It means the image's **width and height change at the same rate**, which **prevents distortion**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Adjusting the aspect ratio keeps the image's original proportions.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Adjusting the aspect ratio **changes the shape and proportions** of the image. Maintaining it is what prevents distortion.

front_blocks.md: Define **cropping**.

back_blocks.md: Cropping is **cutting out and discarding parts of an image**, keeping only the selected portion.

cards.front_md: Define **cropping**.
cards.back_md: Cropping is **cutting out and discarding parts of an image**, keeping only the selected portion.

front_blocks.md: Rotating an image means turning it around a <u>**        **</u> point.

back_blocks.md: Rotating an image means turning it around a **central** point.

front_blocks.md: Which rotations are most commonly offered by software?

back_blocks.md: Software allows rotation to **any angle**, and commonly offers **90 degrees** and **180 degrees** as options.

cards.front_md: Which rotations are most commonly offered by software?
cards.back_md: Software allows rotation to **any angle**, and commonly offers **90 degrees** and **180 degrees** as options.

front_blocks.md: Define **reflecting** an image.

back_blocks.md: Reflecting, or **flipping**, an image means creating a **mirror image of the original**.

cards.front_md: Define **reflecting** an image.
cards.back_md: Reflecting, or **flipping**, an image means creating a **mirror image of the original**.

front_blocks.md: In which two directions can an image be flipped?

back_blocks.md: An image can be flipped **horizontally**, from left to right, or **vertically**, from top to bottom.

cards.front_md: In which two directions can an image be flipped?
cards.back_md: An image can be flipped **horizontally**, from left to right, or **vertically**, from top to bottom.

front_blocks.md: What is the difference between brightness and contrast?

back_blocks.md: **Brightness** affects **all pixels equally**, making the image lighter or darker. **Contrast** adjusts the **difference between light and dark values**, making the image appear more or less detailed.

cards.front_md: What is the difference between brightness and contrast?
cards.back_md: **Brightness** affects **all pixels equally**, making the image lighter or darker. **Contrast** adjusts the **difference between light and dark values**, making the image appear more or less detailed.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Adjusting brightness changes all pixels in the image equally.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
**Brightness** affects all pixels in the image equally, making the whole image **lighter or darker**.

**True or False?**

front_blocks.md: What is the difference between grouping and layering images?

back_blocks.md: **Grouping** combines images so they can be **moved or transformed as a single unit**, while **layering** places images **on top of each other**.

cards.front_md: What is the difference between grouping and layering images?
cards.back_md: **Grouping** combines images so they can be **moved or transformed as a single unit**, while **layering** places images **on top of each other**.

front_blocks.md: How can layered images be reordered?

back_blocks.md: The order can be changed by moving an image to the **front** or to the **back**.

cards.front_md: How can layered images be reordered?
cards.back_md: The order can be changed by moving an image to the **front** or to the **back**.

front_blocks.md: Define **file compression**.

back_blocks.md: File compression is **reducing the size of a file** so that it **takes up less storage space** and makes **file transmission faster**.

cards.front_md: Define **file compression**.
cards.back_md: File compression is **reducing the size of a file** so that it **takes up less storage space** and makes **file transmission faster**.

front_blocks.md: Which element of a file is often the largest?

back_blocks.md: **Images** are often the largest element of a file.

cards.front_md: Which element of a file is often the largest?
cards.back_md: **Images** are often the largest element of a file.

front_blocks.md: What two ways can an image be resized or resampled to reduce file size?

back_blocks.md: By **reducing the resolution** and by **reducing the colour depth**.

cards.front_md: What two ways can an image be resized or resampled to reduce file size?
cards.back_md: By **reducing the resolution** and by **reducing the colour depth**.

front_blocks.md: Define **resolution**.

back_blocks.md: Resolution is the **total amount of pixels that make up an image**.

cards.front_md: Define **resolution**.
cards.back_md: Resolution is the **total amount of pixels that make up an image**.

front_blocks.md: How is the resolution of an image calculated?

back_blocks.md: Resolution is calculated by **multiplying the height and width** of the image in pixels.

cards.front_md: How is the resolution of an image calculated?
cards.back_md: Resolution is calculated by **multiplying the height and width** of the image in pixels.

front_blocks.md: What is the effect of a higher resolution?

back_blocks.md: In general, the **higher the resolution the more detail** there is in the image, so the **higher the quality**.

cards.front_md: What is the effect of a higher resolution?
cards.back_md: In general, the **higher the resolution the more detail** there is in the image, so the **higher the quality**.

front_blocks.md: How does reducing the resolution reduce file size?

back_blocks.md: Reducing the resolution **decreases the number of pixels**, which reduces the file size.

cards.front_md: How does reducing the resolution reduce file size?
cards.back_md: Reducing the resolution **decreases the number of pixels**, which reduces the file size.

front_blocks.md: Define **colour depth**.

back_blocks.md: Colour depth is the **number of bits stored per pixel** in an image.

cards.front_md: Define **colour depth**.
cards.back_md: Colour depth is the **number of bits stored per pixel** in an image.

front_blocks.md: How does reducing the colour depth reduce file size?

back_blocks.md: Reducing the colour depth means **using fewer bits**, and therefore **fewer colours**, which reduces the file size.

cards.front_md: How does reducing the colour depth reduce file size?
cards.back_md: Reducing the colour depth means **using fewer bits**, and therefore **fewer colours**, which reduces the file size.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Reducing resolution or colour depth has no effect on image quality.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Reducing either one can cause a **loss of image quality**, especially when the image is viewed at larger sizes.
